claims.claim: EnterpriseRAG-Bench document Recall@10 = 81.10 on 511,962 docs, 470 evaluable questions
claims.values: Overall 81.10 (BM25 68.4, Vector 46.0, Bash Agent 55.8); 470 of 500 questions have doc labels

claims.claim: Per-category EnterpriseRAG-Bench
claims.values: Semantic n=125: SAG2 58.40 (BM25 43.2, Vector 24.8, Bash 29.6); Conflicting information n=20: 92.50 (BM25 82.5, Vector 55.0, Bash 72.5)
claims.limits: n=20 for conflict

claims.claim: MuSiQue ablation (Figure 4)
claims.values: BM25 54.41; BM25+JEV (H=0) 67.93; H=1 83.36; H=2 86.62; shared scoring context removed 76.25
claims.limits: figure caption has panels (a) expansion depth (b) budget-matched (c) shared context

claims.claim: Budget-matched control: one-shot BM25+JEV vs SAG2
claims.values: BM25+JEV 69.82 at 329,194 judgments vs SAG2 86.62 at 331,325 judgments
claims.limits: one corpus

claims.claim: MuSiQue was also used during method development; subsets fixed dev subsets; synthetic enterprise corpus; hosted JEV not on-prem
claims.quote: MuSiQue was also used during method development.
claims.values: four-hop MuSiQue complete-evidence coverage only 28.31%; cost study single corpus; JEV architecture/weights not public at study time

claims.claim: GPT placed the MuSiQue-development caveat in §4.1
claims.values: §4.1 covers subsets and corpus pooling only; the caveat is in §5.5

claims.claim: Repo README: official reproduction code, extra rows beyond paper
claims.values: SAG2+Jina local rerank 72.13/86.95/97.00; Agentic SAG2 'best historical' 95.39/99.88/99.65 (LLM controller, historical runs); MIT license
claims.limits: Jina reranker weights CC BY-NC 4.0; commit dates not shown

claims.claim: SAG2 indexing cost and author
claims.values: 11,656 MuSiQue passages indexed in 2.36 s, 25.87 MiB SQLite, no model calls; single author Yuchao Wu; v1 2026-10-15

claims.claim: 938 real checks: 670 result-scoring + 268 sentence-check requests, ~9,300 decisions; 100 known negatives
claims.values: 938 flows; 670+268; ~9,300 decisions; tests run 2026-10-02 AEST
claims.limits: vendor that uses Jev in production

claims.claim: Result-relevance AUC (2,228 items)
claims.values: Jev .899; Clef .894; Clef-flash .873; Liquid d1 .905; Perplexity .907
claims.limits: relevance labels produced automatically by answer-key matching, described by the page as noisy

claims.claim: Answerable-gate AUC (647 items)
claims.values: Jev .983; Clef .982; Clef-flash .979; d1 .984; Perplexity .982
claims.limits: only 12 'no' labels plus 100 mismatched-result negatives; labels are the team's own judgements

claims.claim: Good answers hidden by the gate at 0.75
claims.values: Jev 22.2%; Clef 7.3%; Clef-flash 6.2%; d1 10.7%; Perplexity 8.0%
claims.limits: page does not formally define 'hidden'; threshold is a design choice per model

claims.claim: Sentence-support AUC on random 50 of 150 labelled pairs
claims.values: Jev .978; Clef .786; Clef-flash .729; d1 .935; Perplexity .970; supported sentences hidden: Jev 4.9%, Clef 34%, d1 0%
claims.limits: labelled by the team; second model agreed 91.3%; other 100 pairs picked where models disagreed; page says Jev-Perplexity gap is within noise

claims.claim: Knowviq discloses it uses Jev; Jev median 98/122 ms, $0.21 per 1,000 calls vs Perplexity 283/445 ms, $1.28
claims.values: Jev 5,088 avg input tokens vs ~32k for d1/Perplexity
claims.limits: Clef latency measured through a local dev proxy

claims.claim: Jev-as-a-Judge authors and affiliation
claims.values: Alden Do Rosario, Kirollos Atef, both CustomGPT.ai; abs page shows no affiliation

claims.claim: 495 claims from LLM-AggreFact dev split (297 supported / 198 unsupported, 11 component datasets); balanced accuracy
claims.values: jev-1.13.0 73.27; GPT-6 Astra low effort 73.83; high effort 74.11; paired diff -0.56, 95% CI [-5.6, 4.5]; exact McNemar p=0.49
claims.limits: not equivalence; dev split only; single run per arm; benchmark contamination not excluded

claims.claim: False-pass on unsupported claims
claims.values: Jev 23.23%; Astra low 14.14%; Astra high 13.13%; gap 9.1 pts, McNemar p=0.000534 (0.005 Holm)

claims.claim: Cost ratio ~187x (modelled, not invoiced)
claims.limits: modelled from token counts and one day's price list; the paper reports no controlled latency

claims.claim: Cascade result and 'confidence gate vs random escalation'
claims.values: cross-fitted gate 29.9% escalated: 74.10% at $2.92/1k vs Astra 73.83% at $8.93; +0.27 vs Astra (CI -3.85 to +4.15, n.s.); random escalation at matched 30.9% budget: 73.36% mean; gate beat random by 0.65-2.51 pts at all budgets but sample cannot separate it from zero; cascade false-verification 19.22%
claims.limits: offline replay of stored predictions
claims.checks_gpt: savings from fewer strong calls; confidence-gated not shown better than random

claims.claim: R1's '0.15 s and 0.36% cost' and '+0.9 points with cascade'
claims.values: no 0.15 s latency (latency not measured); cost ratio 187x ~= 0.54% of Astra; no +0.9 figure found (nearest: 0.8-point pass-to-pass drift, 0.65-2.51 gate-over-random range)
claims.limits: last 71k chars of HTML not read

claims.claim: SciFact nDCG@10 hybrid order 71.67 -> Jev 1.13 79.29
claims.values: +7.62 pts, 95% CI +4.88 to +10.38 (300 claims, 5,183 abstracts, paired bootstrap 5,000)

claims.claim: Jev vs NVIDIA cross-encoder
claims.values: SciFact: NVIDIA 78.70; Jev +0.59, CI -1.25 to +2.42 (README calls a tie); XQuAD (1,190 q, baseline 98.1%): NVIDIA +0.45
claims.limits: decision-layer analyses exploratory; free-tier runs; repo not affiliated with TypeSafe
claims.checks_gpt: not significantly better than a dedicated cross-encoder

claims.claim: LargitData multi-turn enterprise decisions
claims.values: 20 conversations x 5 turns = 100 decisions; 6 KBs, 8 docs, 6 tools; joint-correct: Gemma 4 31B 77.0%, Jev 1.13.0 61.4%, djev-spark 32.2%, SemIf 24.0%, Laya 322M 0.0%; p50 749 ms vs 2,293 ms; p95 818 vs 4,723
claims.limits: vendor-run, small, Jev hosted vs Gemma self-hosted

claims.claim: Jev weakness: restrictions persisting across turns
claims.values: restriction accuracy Jev 84.4% vs Gemma 95.0%; route 90.6/90.0, scope 85.8/87.0, mode 91.6/92.0; clarifying question when info missing: Gemma 43%, Jev 31%
claims.checks_gpt: weakness in carrying constraints across turns

claims.claim: EnterpriseRAG-Bench corpus and question counts
claims.values: 511,962 documents (abstract says ~500,000); 500 questions in 10 categories: Basic 175, Semantic 125, Intra-Doc 40, Project Related 40, Constrained 30, Conflicting Info 20, Completeness 20, Miscellaneous 20, Info Not Found 20, High Level 10; plus 100 metadata-dependent questions released separately
claims.limits: synthetic company 'Redwood Inference'; gold labels revisable

claims.claim: Source systems: nine
claims.values: Slack ~275k, Gmail ~120k, Linear ~35k, Drive ~25k, HubSpot ~15k, Fireflies ~10k, GitHub ~8k, Jira ~6k, Confluence ~5k (paper: Slack ~285K, Gmail ~121K)
claims.limits: GPT list of Slack/Gmail/GitHub/Jira/Confluence is a subset; Linear, Drive, HubSpot, Fireflies also present

claims.claim: GPT category names differ from source labels
claims.values: 'cross-project' = Project Related (40); 'conflict' = Conflicting Info (20); 'non-existent' = Info Not Found (20); constrained 30; completeness 20

claims.claim: Benchmark baselines and noise design
claims.values: BM25 correctness 68.8, completeness 56.0, recall 68.4; Vector (text-embedding-3-large) 51.4/42.9/46.0; Bash Agent 60.6/61.1/55.8; 8% misfiled docs; near-duplicate conflicts where newer supersedes older; license MIT; leaderboard external on HF

claims.claim: China Mobile / Jiutian Research EnterpriseRAG: 983 expert-validated samples, 6 domains, 13 LLMs
claims.values: 983 samples from 491 Chinese production queries; domains Energy, Medical, Legal, Financial, Party Building, Web Search; conditions noisy retrieval 447, knowledge gaps 227, factual conflicts 309; judge Kimi-k2-thinking kappa 0.77 vs human
claims.limits: benchmark not yet released (raw logs never; desensitized benchmark promised 'upon publication'); LLM judge

claims.claim: Orchestration gap: ~80% per-constraint vs 26.8% all-constraints
claims.values: abstract: ~80% individual vs 26.8% all; body: best model Qwen3-235B-Thinking 83.8% loose vs 26.8% strict, 57-point gap; knowledge-gap refusal best 42.7% (Claude-Opus-4.5); conflict recognition <45% (DeepSeek-R1 44.3%, GPT-4.1 18.5%)
claims.limits: 26.8% attached to the best model in the body, not an average over 13 models; the abstract wording is ambiguous

claims.claim: Arize decision-model benchmark exists (8 models; RAGTruth, Phoenix evaluators, routing)
claims.values: RAGTruth 2,675 rows (wording test 1,338); balanced acc Jev 85.5, Clef 27B 85.2, Liquid d1 84.8, OpenAI Decisions 81.5, Jeeves 9B 80.3, Kev 9B 76.8, Strands 2B 69.0, Laya 59.8; Phoenix 655 cases (Jev 91.1); routing 52 cases (Jev 49/52); calibration error Jev 0.023; Jev p50 0.08 s, $0.045/1k; LLM judge Opus 5 86.6%
claims.limits: Arize is a vendor and integrates Jev; accuracy is on held-out half at each model's tuned cutoff; routing only 52 cases; OpenAI tested in a prompt layout the authors chose

claims.claim: Arize wording sensitivity
claims.values: hallucination question rephrase ROC AUC: Jev 0.93/0.93, Clef 27B 0.92/0.91, Liquid d1 0.92 -> 0.17; Laya 0.11 vs 0.87 on reversed phrasing; option-order not tested

claims.claim: JevBench is a Benchmark Heaven benchmark; versions differ
claims.values: v1.5.4: 1,624 decisions (904 open, 720 sealed), tasks Choice/Noul/Score; official score = harmonic composite of intelligence, calibration, speed, cost; ranks: Cygnet 73.70, Winnow-12B Q8 73.23, Jev 1.13.0 72.13; scores are chance-corrected index, not % accuracy; page retrieved 2026-10-19
claims.limits: BenchLM mirror; ground-truth source not stated; an earlier v1.3.0 (534 decisions, 52 systems, Jev 74.4 first) is known only from search snippet of an aggregator (zeli.app)

claims.claim: Decision Index (HF Space) is a community index, not Kev's own
claims.values: unofficial HF Space by apolinario (multimodalart); 70 models on 38 benchmarks in five weighted areas; Jev reference 57.91; Kev 9B 38.48; scoring code MIT; JevBench 1,624 decisions
claims.limits: secondary Korean write-up

claims.claim: Kev README uses the Decision Index as a column
claims.values: held-out Decision Index: Kev-0.8B 23.3, 4B 38.0, 9B 41.0, 27B 52.3, Jev 54.0 (breadth-v1, 14 public datasets, chance-corrected); transfer-v4 764 records; Kev-27B new-source accuracy 0.889 test vs Jev 0.857 dev; Jev only run on dev sets, training data unknown
claims.limits: not a controlled comparison per README; Apache-2.0

claims.claim: Artificial Analysis also publishes a 'Decision Index' (different thing)
claims.values: weights: AA-Omniscience-Decision accuracy 12.5, non-hallucination 12.5, HLE-MultiChoice 25, When2Call 25, WildGuardTest 25; d1-ultra 65.2, Jev 1.13 57.5, Jev 1.14 57.1, Clef 48.6 (13 models, snapshot 2026-10-19)
claims.limits: secondary mirror; name clash with the HF Space index

claims.claim: NanoJev: 0.6B open decision model (Qwen3-0.6B + decision heads), MIT
claims.values: game tasks on 274-case test set: NanoJev Maze 4/10, Snake 8/8, ViZDoom Basic 128/128, Predict Position 27/128; Jev 7/10, 8/8, 56/128, 11/128
claims.limits: game tasks, not retrieval; README callout links System1-Arena (arXiv 2610.21244)

claims.claim: System1-Arena is a benchmark paper (arXiv 2610.21244), not a NanoJev feature
claims.values: 92,125 typed questions, 105 tasks, 268 public sources, 138 closed-loop envs; 30 models (7 closed LLM, 13 open LLM, 10 System-1); metrics accuracy, Brier, latency, cost, closed-loop success; domains include retrieval, LLM-as-judge, safety, routing, forecasting; CC BY 4.0
claims.limits: retrieval/answerability/evidence tasks not itemized in the text read

claims.claim: System1-Arena headline numbers
claims.values: Jev 72.6% non-agentic accuracy, Brier 0.349, ~321 ms, zero output tokens; agent steps 67.8%, closed-loop 17.4%; Claude Opus 5.5 81.1% / Brier 0.232; Decision-2.0-Vega-27B 73.0%; forecasting hardest

claims.claim: Evidence-sufficiency experiment: only JevRAG (third-party package)
claims.values: HotpotQA val n=300 / test n=700: exact match 0.4129 gated vs 0.4057 fixed baseline, McNemar p=0.36 (n.s.); retrieval rounds -38.5%; ECE 0.3322; answer-abstain test n=300 tie
claims.limits: data and index in a private checkout, not downloadable; single-author package

claims.claim: No domain-classifier comparison of Jev found by that name; nearest items
claims.values: query classification agreement with LLM baseline: Jev zero-shot 66.8%, fine-tuned Laya 74.5%; routing 751 entries Jev P 97.6 / R 98.7 vs baseline 95.6/93.4; reranking 4,855 queries Jev Recall@1 24.37% vs production 35.74% (worse); citation-support judging: Jev most repeatable
claims.limits: Glean says no domain classification experiment; sample sizes partly unstated

claims.claim: Banking77 and classic-classifier comparison (secondhand)
claims.values: Banking77: trained 22M encoder+LR 93.2%, Jev zero-shot 80.1%; Yelp Jev 67.2 vs trained 51.9; Jev ~88% confidence vs ~80% accuracy
claims.limits: explicitly secondhand; no named original

claims.claim: Amplitude analysis: Jev as first stage of a cascade
claims.values: Amplitude benchmark 64 synthetic charts: Jev precision 55.8%, recall 100%, $0.06/1k, 0.14 s; AY Automate 791 decisions, cascade gated at 0.80 matched frontier accuracy at ~1/4 cost; BANKING77 pilot 87.4% confidence vs 75.3% accuracy; jevbench 60-case tool-call 91.7%
claims.limits: synthetic; Amplitude sells Agent Analytics

claims.claim: Rao & Callison-Burch: decision models as rubric judges
claims.values: 9 panels from 7 benchmarks, 27 comparisons; LLM judges 16-357x cost, 5-350x latency; decision models significantly behind in at most 6 of 27; >85% of LLM verdicts repeat the decision model's most confident errors; cascade gain <= 2.7 pts
claims.limits: abstract only read; arXiv search snippet quoted slightly different ranges (29-325x, 8 of 27) from v3 abstract

claims.claim: Deusser et al.: 37-dataset zero-shot evaluation of jev-1.13.0
claims.values: 346,009 requests under USD 10; beats Qwen3.8-27B on 27/37, Gemma-4-E4B on 37/37; Belebele 86.7%; choice probabilities well calibrated, binary poorly vs fixed 0.5 (UNFAIR-ToS micro-F1 0.50 -> 0.75 with tuned threshold); option rotation leaves accuracy unchanged

claims.claim: Akita comparison of 23 decision/classifier models
claims.values: v1 13 policy tasks (130 scenarios x4); v2 7 semantic tasks EN+PT (504 per model); compact v2: Perplexity Decider 27B 99.4, Jev 97.6 (255 ms, ~$0.19/10k), Microsoft Decision-1 97.6, Clef 95.8, OpenAI Decisions 90.5; includes 'evidence support' and 'search relevance' tasks
claims.limits: cases AI-assisted, not independently annotated

claims.claim: Featherless Simple-Jev evaluations: caveats
claims.values: JevBench public set 231 decisions; Jev 200/231 (86.58%) published, 199/231 on rerun; decision benchmarks 33,099 questions; open-model prompts chosen on a 477-case dev set so not held-out
claims.limits: per-model table not extracted

claims.claim: JevBench preprint (preprints.org 202610.0181) could not be read
claims.values: HTTP 403

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: Jev-as-a-Judge is from a 'CMU team'; '0.15 s and 0.36% cost'; '+0.9 points with cascade'
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Authors are Alden Do Rosario and Kirollos Atef at CustomGPT.ai. The paper reports ~187x modelled cost ratio (0.54%), no controlled latency, and cascade +0.27 vs Astra (74.10 vs 73.83, n.s.). No +0.9 or 0.15 s figure found in the first 100k chars; the final 71k were not read.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: SAG2 limitation about MuSiQue development use sits in §4.1 and §5.5
gpt_discrepancies.finding: The caveat is only in §5.5 (Discussion and limitations); §4.1 covers subsets and corpus pooling. All SAG2 numbers (86.62, 97.43, 99.00, 81.10, ablation, budget-matched 69.82) match the paper. Single author; JEV is hosted; README also lists an 'Agentic SAG2 best historical' row (95.39) not in the paper main table.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: Knowviq: 'sentence support AUC .978/.786/.970 (50 labelled samples)', 'hidden correct answers 22.2%/7.3%/8.0%'
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Numbers confirmed, but context matters: Knowviq uses Jev in production; relevance labels came from noisy answer-key string matching; answerability has only 12 'no' labels plus 100 mismatched negatives; 150 sentence pairs labelled, only 50 random; Jev's relevance AUC is below Perplexity and d1.

26.8% is the strict score of the best model (Qwen3-235B-Thinking, 83.8% loose) in the body, not an average over 13 models; abstract wording is ambiguous. Authors are Jiutian Research, China Mobile; benchmark not yet released.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: EnterpriseRAG-Bench categories: cross-project 40, constrained 30, conflict 20, completeness 20, non-existent 20; sources Slack, Gmail, GitHub, Jira, Confluence
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Counts correct; source labels are 'Project Related', 'Conflicting Info', 'Info Not Found'. Nine sources total (also Linear, Drive, HubSpot, Fireflies). Paper Table 9 gives 511,962 docs; README says slightly over 500,000 and slightly different per-source volumes.

Arize benchmark is real (Jim Bennett, October 2026, 8 models) but Arize is a vendor that integrates Jev, so 'independent' is not established. A separate claim that threshold-tuned Jev matched Claude Opus 5 at 87% at ~1/300 cost came from a search snippet only and was not verified.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: CHAT turn 8: 'Kev's Decision Index' and 'NanoJev's System1-Arena'
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Decision Index is a community HF Space (apolinario/multimodalart), which Kev's README adopts as a score column (Kev-27B 52.3 vs Jev 54.0). System1-Arena is a separate paper (arXiv 2610.21244, 2026-10-15, Tianyu Chen et al., 92k questions) that the NanoJev README links to. Artificial Analysis separately publishes a different 'Decision Index'.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: CHAT turn 8: 'domain classifier comparisons' and 'evidence sufficiency experiment'
gpt_discrepancies.finding: No source found with those exact experiments. Nearest: Glean (query classification, routing, reranking, citation support), MindStudio (secondhand Banking77), Akita (includes 'evidence support' task) for classifiers; only the third-party jevrag package for evidence sufficiency (EM 0.4129 vs 0.4057, n.s., -38.5% rounds, private data).

Version dependent: v1.5.4 (1,624 decisions, 2026-10-19 BenchLM mirror) ranks Jev 1.13.0 third (72.13) behind Cygnet and Winnow-12B Q8; the first-place claim (74.4, 534 decisions, v1.3.0) rests on an aggregator snippet only. Scores are chance-corrected composites, not accuracy.

gaps: Jev-as-a-Judge HTML final 71k chars not read; '+0.9 points' and '0.15 s' absent only from the first 100k chars.
SAG2 and other arXiv HTML pages were read through a summarizing fetch tool, not raw tables; numbers cross-checked between paper and README only.
System1-Arena and China Mobile HTML: only first ~100k chars read; System1-Arena retrieval/answerability task list not itemized.
JevBench primary (Benchmark Heaven) page and original v1.3.0 not reached; preprints.org JevBench paper returned 403; Artificial Analysis primary page not reached (BenchLM mirror only).

Many dataset licenses are not stated on arXiv pages; those given come from repos/dataset cards (CRAG CC BY-NC 4.0, RGB CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, LLM-AggreFact CC-BY-ND 4.0 evaluation-only gated). Not found: FEVER, TimeQA, SummaC, AlignScore, MTEB, C-MTEB dataset licenses; FreshQA and RGB sizes; FRAMES paper-page size (HF card gives 824).
CORAL dataset license ambiguous on README.
TREC RAG: no topic counts or dataset license read; official nugget/support evaluation details not confirmed from pages read. Page contained a banner aimed at AI agents; ignored.
Knowviq label provenance beyond what the page states is unknown; Arize 'Opus 5 at 87%/1/300 cost' and Amplitude/other secondary claims partly from search snippets.
Part 2 catalog has 27 entries; MTEB reranking, SummaC and AlignScore are listed as framework/metric entries, not full datasets.
